The Washington Times

Saturday, September 26, 2026

The [Supreme Court](/topics/supreme-court/) rejected [Republicans](/topics/republicans/)’ latest try to revive a GOP-tilted map for November’s congressional elections, ruling for a third time that even though the state held primaries under the new map, the old one must be used.

In an unsigned order, the court said state law requires the old map’s use, and the fact that the election is so near also argues for using the old map, which was applied in 2022 and 2024.

“At this late date, ordering reversion to the 2025 map in the midst of an ongoing election would usher in electoral chaos,” the justices said.

At stake is likely the outcome of one seat.

Under the old map, Democrats won two of the state’s eight seats in the U.S. House. [Republicans](/topics/republicans/) hoped to reduce Democrats to just one seat with the new map, which eliminates the Kansas City-based district of Rep. Emanuel Cleaver II.
